title: Daily Market Digest: September 27, 2026
subtitle: Review of Friday, September 25, 2026, Trading Session - Markets Closed Today

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Conclude Week Higher Amid Easing Oil Prices and Yields
items.summary: U.S. equities closed out their first winning week in three on Friday, September 25, 2026, with major indices posting gains. A cooldown in oil prices and a slight ease in Treasury yields helped to alleviate some market pressures, despite lingering concerns about inflation and potential Fed actions. AI-related technology stocks continued to be a significant driving force for market growth. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Surges on AI Demand
items.summary: Dell Technologies ($DELL) opened up 3.63% on Friday, rebounding from earlier selling pressures. The rise was attributed to exceptionally strong demand for its AI servers and the company's raised full-year guidance.

items.headline: Costco Rises on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Costco Wholesale ($COST) climbed 2.9% after the retailer reported stronger-than-expected profit for its latest quarter, serving as a positive catalyst for Friday's trading.

items.headline: Akamai Pops on Major Cloud Deal
items.summary: Akamai ($AKAM) saw a significant pop of +19.1% following news of signing an $11.6 billion seven-year cloud deal with Anthropic. This move was noted in after-hours trading from Thursday, influencing Friday's open.

items.headline: Energy Sector Lags as Crude Prices Fall
items.summary: The energy sector was the worst-performing, lagging with a 0.88% loss, primarily due to falling Brent crude oil prices, which declined 2% to $104 per barrel. Notable decliners included Devon Energy ($DVN), ONEOK ($OKE), Occidental Petroleum ($OXY), APA ($APA), and EQT ($EQT).

items.headline: Technology Leads, Energy Lags in Friday's Sector Performance
items.summary: Information Technology was the top-performing sector, gaining 0.99% for the day, with strength in semiconductor and AI-related stocks. Communication Services and Healthcare also saw gains. Conversely, the Energy sector lagged with a 0.88% loss, and Materials and Utilities sectors also showed weakness.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data Released; Consumer Inflation Expectations Rise
items.summary: U.S. new home sales in August jumped 6.4% to an annualized rate of 684,000 units, reaching the highest level since December 2025. Meanwhile, the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey for September edged down to -2 from 4 in August. The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment report indicated that consumers expect inflation to be 4.6% in the coming year, an increase from the previous month's 4% forecast.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Approaches with Strong Growth Expectations
items.summary: As the third-quarter earnings season draws near, S&P 500 earnings are projected to increase by 23.9% year-over-year. This marks the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index, driven significantly by the Aerospace, Energy, and Technology sectors.
